summary: Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.
Bror Fredrik Tiliander (1896–1990) specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Lund University, with Helmer Smith, and earned his PhD at Uppsala University (around 1968–1974).

Bruce B. Lawrence (born 1941) works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Fay School, Princeton University (~1962–1965), and Episcopal Divinity School (~1966–1969), later serving as Professor (~1971–2008) and Emeritus Professor (~2008) at Duke University.

Bruce Cameron Hall is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1980. In 1987, he was attested as an assistant editor at the College of William & Mary.

Bruce Charles Williams specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.
Bruce Chilton (born 1949) is a religious studies scholar who studied at St John's College (~1971–1977). He held a post at Yale University (~1985–1987) and became Director at Bard College around 1987.

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD at Columbia University (attested 1983) under Alex Wayman, also studying with Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Kapferer (born 1940) studied at the University of Sydney (~1959–1963) and University of Manchester (~1963–1969). He held positions at the universities of Adelaide (~1975–1985), UCL (~1985–1999), Bergen (~1999), Gothenburg, and James Cook University.

Bruce Lincoln (born 1948) works in religious studies and history. After Haverford and a PhD at Chicago (~1970–1976) under Mircea Eliade, he held posts at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1993).
Bruce M. Knauft (born 1954) studied at the University of Michigan (~1977–1983). Around 1986, he was appointed Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology at Emory University.

Bruce M. Sullivan (born 1951) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (1976–1984), where he studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen, and became Professor Emeritus at Northern Arizona University.

Bruce Matthews (born 1941) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who did graduate work at McMaster University (~1970–1974). He held posts at the University of Ceylon and as Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1988) and has served as associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens (1935–2023), who studied under Colette Caillat, worked in Indology and archaeology. He held posts at EFEO (1969), KU Leuven (1972–1977), French Institute of Pondicherry (1977), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich (1862–1939) studied at Munich, Göttingen, and Breslau, earning a doctorate under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Wrocław University Library, Heidelberg University (1912; ~1918–1928), and the University of Breslau, becoming Professor of Indology (1921–1928).

Bruno Lindner (1853–1930) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Jena under teachers including Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Windisch. From 1878 to 1919, he served as Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig.

Bruno Meissner (1868–1947) studied at the universities of Leipzig (~1888–1890) and Strasbourg (~1890–1892). He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1904–1920) and the University of Berlin (~1920–1935).

Bruno Petzold (1873–1949) studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and under Shinsho Hanayama and Daito Shimaji. He held teaching posts in Japan at the First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Seikei High School, and Rissho University (~1928–1944).

Bruno Schindler (1882–1964) was a Sinologist who earned his doctorate under August Conrady (~1913–1919). He founded the journal Asia Major in 1923 and worked as a publisher's reader at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).
